title: NVIDIA Unveils 2.8T-Token Indic Pretraining Corpus and Open Pipeline
source_used: Unite.AI (reporting an NVIDIA and AI4Bharat announcement)
key_facts: NVIDIA, with IIT Madras and its AI4Bharat lab, introduced Nemotron-pretraining-Indic-v1 on 16 Oct 2026; the corpus is 'releasing soon'.
It holds about 2.8 trillion tokens of synthetic (machine-translated) text across the 22 languages listed in India's Constitution.
The 22 languages are the first language of 97% of Indians, per the announcement.
The open data-generation pipeline (prompts, workflows, quality checks) is released so developers can adapt it.
Translations are scored by Gemma-4-31B-it and kept only at 75 out of 100 or higher; the translator also acts as judge for twelve languages.
Continued pretraining with Indic data raised scores on five Indic benchmarks by 4.98 to 9.82 percentage points; NVIDIA says this does not isolate the synthetic corpus's effect.
AI4Bharat also released Indic-LLM-Eval-Suite, an open benchmark collection.
NVIDIA cautions translated text does not replace native-written text and may contain errors; quality checking is mainly automated.
quote_evidence: Khapra, who heads AI4Bharat, has named the core problem: "we do not have enough data for Indian languages."
NVIDIA cautions that translation does not replace text originally written in Indian languages or guarantee coverage of local knowledge and culture.
The post states that retained text can still contain errors.
why_it_matters_hint: Aims at the shortage of training data for Indian languages, with candid limits.
notes: Company announcement relayed by Unite.AI; benchmark gains are NVIDIA's own claims. Corpus not yet released at time of report.
